reason: The cited evidence shows that LPBF parameters can control microstructure (E1), that rapid cooling and short melt durations occur in laser processing (E3), that lower energy input reduces cracking (E4), and that nonequilibrium SRO can form during rapid solidification (E5). However, no evidence directly links pulse modulation to SRO formation in AlCrFeNiSi, nor demonstrates that SRO reduces residual stress or improves mechanical properties in this system; the specific pulse parameters are unsupported.
premises: Pulse-modulated laser scanning reduces thermal gradients during LPBF solidification
Reduced thermal gradients promote nonequilibrium short-range order (SRO) formation
Nonequilibrium SRO alleviates residual stresses and reduces microstructural defects
Lower residual stresses and fewer defects improve yield and fatigue strengths
The proposed pulse parameters (50 µs pulse, 150 µs dwell) are effective for AlCrFeNiSi
